title: Rosalind and the Cellar
premise: When Juniper Villalobos returns to his grandmother's house to bury his twin brother Rosalind, he finds the family photographs altered: an empty chair has appeared in every image, and the cellar below holds the records of a founding ritual the town's first families never finished. As the chair moves closer to the camera in each new photograph, Juniper realizes the ritual demands a twin to complete it, and Rosalind's death was the opening move. Racing the solstice deadline, Juniper must choose between destroying the founders' ledger and finishing the rite himself, which would bind him to the house forever. In the end, he burns the ledger and takes the chair's place willingly, trading his memory of belonging for his sister's peace, and the photographs finally show only the family that remains.
about_author: M. M. Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales in rural New England, where they developed a professional unease about family photographs. They write horror about houses that keep records.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He arrives at grandma's house with Rosalind's ashes, grieving and guilty, having been the twin who left. While sorting the attic for the funeral, he notices every old photograph now contains an extra wooden chair that no one remembers. The emotional beat is dislocation: home should be familiar, but the house is quietly correcting itself around him.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Obsessively photographing the house to track the chair's movement, he finds the cellar and the founders' ledger, which describes a solstice ritual requiring 'two made one.' His aunt denies everything, but her own childhood photos show her standing beside the chair. The beat is dread deepening into compulsion as his documentation becomes the ritual's map.

chapters.title: What the Chair Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, fractured by the house's borrowed memories. Sitting in the chair, he experiences the founders' ceremony and learns the ritual was abandoned mid-binding, leaving the house hungry for a twin ever since. Rosalind's death wasn't an accident; the house chose her. The beat is horror turning to rage as he understands he was meant to be the offering.

chapters.title: Two Made One
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, solstice night. The founders' descendants arrive to finish the ritual with him in the chair, but Juniper has memorized the ledger's inversion: he burns it while seated, unbinding the house by giving up his memories of belonging rather than his life. The chair empties, the photographs settle, and he leaves carrying only the feeling that he was loved, without the proof.
